summary.name: Neuralink
summary.one_liner: Neuralink is a brain-computer interface company whose implant translates neural signals into actions, currently being tested in clinical trials with people controlling computers and robotic arms by thought.
use_cases: operating a robotic arm with neural signals
assistive technology for people with paralysis
participating in a brain implant clinical trial
summary.what_it_does: Neuralink develops a brain-computer interface that reads neural signals and translates them into actions. According to the page, participants in its clinical trials use Neuralink devices to control computers and robotic arms with their thoughts. The stated goal is to restore autonomy to people with unmet medical needs and to unlock new dimensions of human potential. The page features testimonials from trial participants with spinal cord injury and ALS, describing creative work, writing, and returning to work. It also has separate calls for patients, caregivers, engineers and operators.
notable: Implant-based brain interface tested in human clinical trials
Controls computers and robotic arms via neural signals
Participant testimonials from people with spinal cord injury and ALS
caveats: Available only through clinical trials as far as the page states
Not a general consumer product; eligibility and availability not stated on the page
